Notes: One row per family, like Evite/Punchbowl. Email/First Name/Last Name are the primary contact (the first adult on the family record); Couple / Family Member 1-6 are every other adult and each kid, formatted as "Name <email>" when that person should get their own emailed invite, or just "Name" when they shouldn't (see the Include kids' email addresses toggle on the app's Invites page). Note the last two headers are both literally "Couple / Family Member 5" - a typo carried over from the original template; the second one is treated as Member 6 positionally.
Description: One invite per family. Everyone else in the household is listed as an extra recipient - kids only get emailed their own copy if you turn that on below.

Notes: No family/group concept offered here - one row per PERSON (parents, kids per the Kids setting, staff), not per family. There's no Invite by choice for this system since there's no group mode to switch to. Evite's own importer wants no header row and just Name/Email/Phone in that order. See https://support.evite.com/products/invitations/manage-and-edit-guest-list/upload-guest-list-excel-spreadsheet
Description: One invite per person, not per family - Evite has no way to represent a household as one invitee here, so everyone (parents, kids per the Kids setting, staff) is addressed on their own. The downloaded file has no header row - that's expected, Evite doesn't want one.

Notes: One OUTPUT ROW PER FAMILY MEMBER, not one per family - unlike the other tabs. Repeat this template row once for each person in the family (the primary contact, any other adults, the kids), filling Name/Email or Phone for that one person each time. Group Name repeats the same {{ greeting }} across every row in the family so Paperless Post clusters them into one couple/family. Email or Phone can be left blank for a member with no contact info of their own. Total Invited and Message are optional and left blank here. See https://paperlesspost.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/206579093
Description: One row per person, not per family - parents and kids all appear separately, but grouped under the family's name so Paperless Post treats them as one invite.
